##### OpenAI and ClawRouter Decisions


An explicit OpenAI Decision evaluation with GPT-6 Luna can include an inline PNG, JPEG or WebP image up to 4 MiB, and Decision V2 keeps the other answers when one question is refused. Evaluations send the supplied evidence to OpenAI and use Platform billing. Use a Platform API key with Decisions access. See [OpenAI Decision models](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/openai#decision-models).

Deployments that serve native Decisions can also select Luna through ClawRouter. Hosted availability was pending as of October 20, 2026, and access depends on the router key and service. See [ClawRouter Decisions setup](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/clawrouter#decision-models) and the [shared plugin SDK entry point](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/sdk-entrypoints.md).
Add image evidence, per-question refusals in V2 and discovery of models configured just for Decisions.

- Adds an opt-in 12-hour prompt cache lifetime for GPT-5.6 and later through the OpenAI Responses API. Twelve-hour writes cost 2.5 times ordinary input, compared with 1.25 times for 30-minute writes, with the same cached-read rate. OpenClaw estimates costs using the lifetimes OpenAI reports. [Cache lifetime guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/prompt-caching#openai-12-hour-cache-lifetime)

- Cuts repeated credential and authentication work across agent turns while settings stay unchanged, and continues to pick up credential changes in scoped environments.
  The changes cover authentication with unchanged plugins, provider credential reuse across turns, and scoped credential lookups.

  [#183868](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183868), [#183889](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183889), [#183990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183990).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces provider lookup and startup work, including Gateway restarts using CLI model providers and Gateways using providers other than Anthropic. A CLI provider available only through plugin setup must be declared by exactly one plugin.
  CLI provider lookup.

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces CPU and temporary memory use while handling model replies, including concurrent streams and completed streams held for rate-limit tracking. OpenAI Responses also does less work deciding whether an interrupted reply can be retried.
  The changes cover streaming when diagnostics have not requested measurements, completed rate-limited streams, concurrent model streams, waiting replies and interrupted Responses recovery.

  [#182963](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182963), [#183342](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183342), [#184222](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184222), [#185517](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185517).

- Reduces processing and temporary memory use while reading streamed replies from providers and MCP servers, including OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and guarded HTTP streams. It also cuts work for eligible delegated streams using the same rate-limit account.
  The changes cover provider and MCP streams, Chat Completions, streams without a rate-limit account or using the delegating request’s account, delegated streams, Responses and guarded HTTP streams.

  [#184103](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184103), [#184190](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184190), [#184564](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184564), [#184595](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184595), [#184605](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184605).

  [#173979](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173979).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes paid Claude CLI usage showing as free when old plugin catalog copies override current prices, and stops saving new copies in your model settings. On affected installs, `openclaw doctor --fix` backs up the settings and removes qualifying exact copies. The cleanup can also remove duplicate model listings and correct a misleading Claude CLI sign-in status. [Doctor state and sessions](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/doctor/state-and-sessions)
  [#174641](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174641).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Restores provider names shown as `***` in older usage and cost reports when Doctor can verify them from session history. Doctor reports entries it leaves masked and cuts repeat scanning during historical transcript repairs. If your usage still shows `***` and the first Doctor pass upgraded the agent database, run `openclaw doctor --fix` again to apply the deferred repair. [Doctor state and sessions](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/doctor/state-and-sessions)
  [#174665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174665).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Fixes agents with a separate state scope failing to save valid OAuth sign-in credentials or refreshed tokens.
  [#174724](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174724).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes provider usage staying blank or stuck on refreshing on the Models page. Reloading the page also reuses recent usage results within the cache window.
  [#174741](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174741).

  [#174752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174752).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

By default, OpenClaw sends the image to the configured vision provider and passes its description to your chosen text model with your extra prompt context. If no description can be produced, check `agents.defaults.imageModel` or an image-capable `tools.media.models` entry before retrying. [Local models](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/local-models)
  [Issue #93741](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93741)

  [#174963](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174963).

- Fixes shared HTTP model discovery and refreshes cutting off slow providers before their configured timeout or waiting longer than requested. The provider timeout is capped by the overall discovery deadline. [Model discovery settings](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/models)
  [#168356](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/168356)

  [#180842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180842).

- Prevents eligible local reasoning sessions using OpenAI-compatible servers such as llama.cpp from losing room for the next reply or trimming conversation history too early after a tool call. The fix uses the previous request’s measured usage when the start of the prompt still matches. It also fixes unchanged structured output schemas being counted twice against the next reply’s space.

The first request also uses Qwen error handling. Token Plan endpoints also apply the model’s thinking limits and rules for carrying reasoning into later requests.

  [#181638](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181638).

- Fixes [fallback models](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-failover) missing their own plugin instructions and receiving the same message and images twice. The fallback gets fresh plugin context for the message.

- Fixes provider requests sending headers that were explicitly removed, even if the original header used different capitalization. This also keeps default authorization off local OpenAI-compatible requests that explicitly opt out. Provider plugins that read runtime headers should preserve `null` as a removal through merges and omit it before sending through a string-only HTTP client. [Provider runtime hooks](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/runtime-hooks)
  Use `omitNullRequestHeaders` after the final merge for string-only HTTP clients.

  [#182351](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182351).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes changes to watched groups invalidating otherwise reusable conversation context. Adding, renaming, or removing a watched group still updates what your agent sees, and compatible providers can reuse the earlier context.

  Thanks [@ensignwesley](https://github.com/ensignwesley) (author) and [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) (contributor).
- Skips the extra model request for a final answer when a scheduled check finishes its work and intentionally stays silent. Keeps requests needed to finish a turn from disturbing the conversation’s prompt cache. [Prompt caching](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/prompt-caching)

- Fixes provider catalogs being skipped during concurrent plugin loading and keeps healthy providers’ models visible when another provider is missing credentials or its catalog hook fails.
  For concurrent plugin loading, see [issue #195477](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/195477).

  [#196448](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196448), [commit 67cc5d9a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/67cc5d9ab485f8a0aafb6236392513b7ad5b9c46).

  [Provider discovery isolation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2b08b6f7880ded69c626f5c63f087517c0802bcd).
- Fixes agent runs waiting past the [retry delay limit](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/retry) after a provider rate limit. If no fallback model is configured and the request is safe to repeat, OpenClaw tries another eligible provider account or returns the error if none remains. If actions cannot safely be repeated, the turn ends with an error instead. Check what finished before retrying.
  For unsafe retries, the cap defaults to 60 seconds; setting it to zero disables it. See [issue #168101](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/168101).

  [#197611](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197611), [commit 37740dc6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/37740dc688913e3a9c3edeffd5bcc9fbb9fec11c).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa) for the release backport, [@kringsc](https://github.com/kringsc) for the report, and [@aron-intframe](https://github.com/aron-intframe), [@abacha](https://github.com/abacha), [@oldrich333](https://github.com/Oldrich333), [@jaxonparrott](https://github.com/jaxonparrott) and [@alexph-dev](https://github.com/alexph-dev) for reproduction and diagnosis.

  For safe retries, profile pins still restrict selection, and setting the cap to zero disables it. See [issue #161981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/161981).

  [commit d0d0f865](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d0d0f86547285fee3eb8d861510d1878b9740deb), [#162398](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162398).

Previously uncounted turns still contribute to token and message counts and cost totals. This doesn’t correct copies made before the update.

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Stops OpenClaw from asking Kilo models to use tools when those models say they don’t support them.
  [report #151015](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/151015).

  [#187365](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187365).

  Thanks [@yousan](https://github.com/yousan), [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus) and [@masatohoshino](https://github.com/masatohoshino).

  [#167251](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167251).

  Thanks [@Alix-007](https://github.com/Alix-007), [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes missing Usage metrics when some turns have no provider usage data. The Usage page, charts, exports and command summaries report measured usage without the old lower-bound label. Turns with unknown usage still count as messages and, if they failed, as errors, but totals can understate what you used or were charged.
  [#187212](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187212).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Fixes interactive [LiteLLM](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/litellm) setup skipping the proxy URL or choosing a model your proxy may not serve. Choose an advertised model or enter an ID; if discovery fails, setup explains why. Signing in again keeps saved provider and model settings, including the proxy address, when provider names differ in capitalization. Activating a saved sign-in no longer brings back duplicate provider entries. If configuration changes during setup, the request stops before credentials go to the old endpoint.
  Proxy setup and provider settings · Model discovery · Reauthentication · [LiteLLM guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/providers/litellm.md).

  Thanks [@midhunvnadh](https://github.com/midhunvnadh) and [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), and [@Hylance](https://github.com/Hylance) for the report.

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

  [#175744](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175744).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

<a id="prompt-caching-and-conversation-continuations-1" />

##### Prompt caching and conversation continuations fixes

- Fixes avoidable [prompt-cache](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/prompt-caching) misses when you continue a conversation, including after background or subagent work, a restart, or a switch between clients. When a subagent finishes while its parent is idle, the handoff is retained in the raw transcript while remaining hidden in chat.
  The fixes cover changing instructions, returned session results, history reloads, Goals and scheduled wakes. Subagent follow-ups retain their role, restrictions and delegation rules. A CLI continuation of a saved group keeps its presentation while using the current reply route; scheduled actions remain limited to the current job. See [Reports and continuation examples](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/143017#issuecomment-6457000585).

  [#185887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185887), [#185888](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185888), [#186208](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186208), [#186338](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186338).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), [@abacha](https://github.com/abacha) for the report, and [@iceteaSA](https://github.com/iceteaSA), [@VishalJ99](https://github.com/VishalJ99) and [@duardor968](https://github.com/duardor968) for continuation examples.

  Eligible internal follow-up turns on native OpenAI Responses and direct Anthropic pinned-prompt routes keep the session’s selected personal preferences; isolated cron jobs use shared defaults. Display-only changes no longer cause false history-change warnings. See the [Endpoint guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/reference/prompt-caching.md).

  Tool permissions still apply immediately. Eligible UI turns keep task suggestions, while incoming turns without a grant do not gain access. Tool search can find the right tool when names overlap, including on remote workers. The changes cover CLI and recovery, the OpenAI client, same-session follow-ups and embedded run history.

  [#181279](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181279), [#181301](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181301), [#183898](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183898), [#185784](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185784).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

  For background completions and tools, see [issue #191128](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191128).

  [#197835](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197835), [commit 2a2c7368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2a2c73689d60e83a66b339a8f1c6a142b9ce2559).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus) and [@mirasrael](https://github.com/mirasrael) for contributing, [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa) for the release backport, and [@exgeni](https://github.com/exGeni) for reproduction.

  For task suggestions, see [issue #155868](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/155868).

  [#197893](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197893), [commit f3eb4cdf](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f3eb4cdff904474619f37147c9e0c33b28169b01).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus) and [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa) (release backport).

  Configured owner guidance remains in the prompt when a subagent finishes, without changing sender authority. See [Issue #180607](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180607) and the [Related cache discussion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150081).

  [#180608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180608).

  Thanks [@masatohoshino](https://github.com/masatohoshino) and [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), Eragim for the broader cache report, and CodeForcer for identifying the owner guidance difference.

  For a completion while the parent is idle, the handoff is retained for the next turn’s history. See [issue #181672](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/181672).

  [#181673](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181673).

  Thanks [@masatohoshino](https://github.com/masatohoshino).
- Fixes repeated prompt-cache writes when session instructions change on affected [Anthropic Messages connections](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/anthropic), including OAuth, custom proxies, Vertex and Foundry. Updated instructions still reach the model, and the session’s starting prompt can be retained across restarts.
  This change does not cover Bedrock Converse or remote worker turns.

  [#197925](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197925), [commit 7c236d45](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7c236d45c0689085ba9cf688aac8c725d4bbebdb).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus) and [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa) (release backport).

#### Automations and Scheduling

Automations can use their creating conversation and run supported watchers in a Docker sandbox. If an automation linked to a removed or archived conversation pauses, restore the conversation and re-enable the job. Before downgrading, stop sandboxed watchers, wait for cleanup and keep a verified backup; older versions quarantine those jobs. Returning to 11.4 after the automation state database upgrade requires a compatible pre-update backup. Heartbeat moves to Automations, where you can change its schedule and delivery.




##### Automations and chat memory


**Automations and chat memory**

Automations can now use information saved in the chat that created them and update that chat’s dashboard, even when they run separately. For example, a weekly family meal-plan automation can use a saved preference for 30-minute dinners and put the plan on the family chat’s dashboard.
Jobs from an owner's direct chat can use owner-private memory while the requester remains an owner; jobs from group or non-owner chats use only that conversation's memory.

If the linked conversation is removed or archived, or its worktree is gone, the next scheduled run is skipped and the job pauses. Command jobs are exempt from this check. Restore the conversation or worktree and run `openclaw automations enable <jobId>` to resume it. A `/new` reset lets the job run without the old conversation's access. See [Automation troubleshooting](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/troubleshooting).

The changes cover dashboard reads, edits and eligible widget pins, and conversation memory within its permission limits. Resetting or removing the conversation cuts off inherited access and new dashboard edits or pins; new edits and pins are also blocked after the run finishes.

[#178965](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178965), [#179011](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179011), [#179062](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179062).

Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).

**Watching logs in a Docker sandbox**

A watcher that follows a shared workspace log can now run in its own supported [local Docker sandbox](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#sandboxed-streams) instead of directly on the host. If an overnight backup writes to that log, you can ask OpenClaw to alert you if it reports a failure, even after you close the chat. When policy asks for approval, it applies to that watcher and does not confirm it started. Before downgrading, stop sandboxed watchers, wait for cleanup and keep a verified backup; older versions quarantine these jobs, and upgrading again does not automatically restore them.
When your execution policy asks for approval, an agent-created Gateway watcher request shows what will run, where it runs, where its output goes and that it can continue after the conversation and restart automatically.

Before downgrading, stop sandboxed streams, wait for them to settle and keep a verified backup. Older versions quarantine these jobs, and upgrading again does not restore them automatically.

Watcher approvals apply to the saved watcher; a refusal leaves an existing watcher unchanged, and reopening the conversation restores a pending request. Approval does not mean it started or stopped.

[#177941](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177941).

Docker sandbox streams start in a fresh dedicated container without falling back to the host.

[#177942](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177942).

Thanks [@joshavant](https://github.com/joshavant) and [@eleqtrizit](https://github.com/eleqtrizit) for both changes.

**Scheduled plugin follow-ups**

A supporting plugin can check on a request later and leave the result in the original conversation without posting to the channel. For example, a parcel-tracking plugin could check a delivery again at 5. From an eligible authenticated command, a plugin can schedule a follow-up once or on a recurring schedule, and OpenClaw checks the original requester's current permissions before each run. See [scheduled plugin commands](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime/background-work#requester-admitted-scheduled-commands).

Newly accepted schedules marked to survive a Gateway restart can continue if the matching plugin code and command remain available. For core-bundled plugins, this also requires the same identifiable packaged build; a different build or a disabled plugin ends the schedule at its next run. An occurrence that may already have started is skipped after restart.
The original deadline and remaining runs are retained across a supported restart. The [background work guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime/background-work) explains eligibility and re-enrollment. Rolling back to a host without the applicable continuity support can retire a schedule at its next occurrence.

The Control UI and full cron details and events identify the plugin and command without showing private arguments. For bundled plugin schedules, see the [manifest capabilities](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/manifest/capabilities).

[#180282](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180282), [#180844](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180844), [#180879](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180879), [#181331](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181331).

Thanks [@fuller-stack-dev](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev).




##### Automations and scheduled work


- **Heartbeat moves to Automations.** Heartbeat is the regular check your agent makes for you. Once your existing check moves, open Automations to change how often it runs, what it checks and where you receive updates. You keep the history of previous runs. See the [Heartbeat migration guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/heartbeat). Managed updates that support Heartbeat migration move compatible checks automatically. If you replace the binary manually, run `openclaw doctor --fix`. Checks can send repeated notifications and still run when there is nowhere to send updates, so review where updates are sent if you relied on the old behavior. Older Gateway versions cannot read the converted data. To roll back, restore a pre-upgrade backup with the matching older build in a separate data directory. If you write plugins using the [removed heartbeat APIs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/removed-surfaces#heartbeat-executor-and-wake-helpers), update them before upgrading OpenClaw.
  Job scratch is included in model context for session-target and standalone scheduled agent runs, so do not put secrets in it.

  Command, task, hook and restart follow-ups that relied on heartbeat now run in ordinary sessions. Device notification changes and background command completions can reach their intended conversation without waiting for a heartbeat. A command result returned directly does not also produce a completion notice. Older Codex threads that still call `heartbeat_respond` may receive an unavailable-tool response.

  Main-session agent-turn jobs retain Announce or owner delivery when edited in the Control UI or CLI. See [delivery guidance](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/delivery).

  If Doctor keeps a conflicting or recreated `HEARTBEAT.md`, review it and copy any instructions you still want into the automation. If Doctor skips an older migrated task that still tries to send a quiet reply, update its prompt to use `NO_REPLY`. See the [Heartbeat migration guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/doctor/config-migrations).

  See the [job scratch guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.5/docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md#L320-L330).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes isolated cron runs using the native Agents API taking too long to report their result or leaving an unused session behind after the run finishes.
  [#180877](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180877).

  Thanks [@yinx65588-boop](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop), [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Fixes scheduled follow-ups losing permission to continue in the same conversation after the owner edits the job or a recurring trigger adds context. Queued follow-ups pick up the latest saved edits when the conversation becomes idle. An authorization failure is shown and stops that follow-up. Restarts and cancellations can still be retried. If an older follow-up’s authorization was captured while it was paused, its owner needs to recreate the follow-up after upgrading.
  [Cron payloads](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md).

  [#180891](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180891).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes scheduled automations losing their final reply when they remove themselves. Removing or disabling an automation from another turn, or pressing Stop, still cancels the run.
  [#181085](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181085).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes automation error links leaving invalid fields hidden. Selecting an error for a field in the collapsed Advanced section opens the section and puts focus on the field so you can correct it.
  [#181218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181218).

  Thanks [@etzelm](https://github.com/etzelm).

  Reviewed by [@shakkernerd](https://github.com/shakkernerd).
- Removes misleading app reauthorization instructions from scheduled Codex jobs that use only MCP tools or otherwise have no app access.
  [#181219](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181219).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

  Reported by [@cbremer](https://github.com/cbremer) ([#180370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180370)).
- Cuts repeated work that put memory pressure on large installations when Doctor migrated model-account settings for older cron jobs.
  [Doctor state and sessions](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/doctor/state-and-sessions)

  [#181293](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181293).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and [@609NFT](https://github.com/609NFT).
- Fixes confirmed [automation results](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/delivery) waiting for an ongoing reply to finish before appearing in the destination conversation. These results no longer hold up a restart just because that reply is still running.
  [#181506](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181506).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes scheduled jobs from an owner’s Discord DM being treated as if the requester wasn’t an owner. Each run checks the requester’s current owner access, including for private memory from the parent conversation when the job uses it.
  [#181916](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181916).

  Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).
- Fixes scheduled tasks dropping subagent replies or waiting past their timeout when the system clock changes during the wait.
  [#182144](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182144).

  Thanks [@xialonglee](https://github.com/xialonglee), [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Stops eligible agent automations created from a Control UI conversation from continuing to use a revoked device or access grant. The next run is refused and the automation is disabled with a reason. If a run is already underway, it loses access to remaining operator-only actions. For an eligible older job, bind it from its parent conversation to record creator access. [Automation payloads](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/payloads)
  [#182348](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182348), [explicit binding follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f3ac84c9a607afabbaea42a4b2dbf16b56757a7).

  Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).
- Corrects what agents are told about scheduling work for the current conversation. A detached run uses the conversation’s saved workspace and sandbox while that conversation is current, falls back to the scheduled agent’s workspace otherwise, and ends if you reset the conversation. Cloud placement follows the scheduled job’s own rules. [How scheduled jobs work](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/how-it-works)
  [#182350](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182350).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Prevents broken characters at the end of last-heartbeat previews for converted command automations when an emoji or other Unicode character crosses the cutoff.
  [#182776](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182776).

  Thanks [@wangmiao0668000666](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666).
- Fixes reminders and other automations failing to save when an agent sends usable settings in the wrong format, whether it is creating an automation or editing an existing one.
  Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) for the fix and [@linuxmum](https://github.com/LinuxMum) for the earlier related proposal. [#182824](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182824) · [#97339](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97339)
- Enforces run-specific permissions for automation tools in webhooks and channel join introductions. Webhook runs stay scoped to their own automation, and channel join introductions run without automation tools.
  [#183913](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183913).

  Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).
- Fixes misleading account mismatch errors in scheduled runs that use a CLI account. The run reports when the credential store needs repair or account setup is cancelled.
  [#184555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184555).

  Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).
- Fixes newly account-bound automations running on the wrong runtime after a session or configuration change. Older bindings without a recorded runtime still choose one the same way. Errors identify the account or runtime when known and tell you how to record an account when needed. Changing accounts within the same provider is refused if the recorded runtime is no longer available.
  [#185070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185070).

  Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).
- Prevents `current` automations with a saved runtime from switching models or failing to run when you change the model or provider in the conversation that created them. Jobs without a saved runtime still follow the conversation’s model selection. To change the scheduled model yourself, use `automations edit --model`.
  [Automation model selection](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/payloads).

  [#185341](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185341).

  Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).
- Fixes older search results replacing the list on the Automations page when a newer search fails. The last accepted list stays visible alongside the error, and you can retry the search.
  [#185466](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185466).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes upgrade checks choosing the wrong set of scheduled jobs when an older updater leaves out the path to a custom configuration and more than one set is saved. Fixes Doctor losing track of which scheduled jobs and heartbeat data to migrate on SQLite installations with a custom configuration.
  [Issue #185457](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/185457)

  [#185723](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185723).

  Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).
- Prevents automatic cleanup from deleting a pinned continuation for an isolated cron run, so you can return to that specific run after it finishes.
  [Issue #185712](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/185712)

  [#185750](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185750).

  Thanks [@geomagilles](https://github.com/geomagilles) and [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Fixes scheduled jobs cutting off long subagent reports when the job delegates the work and sends no reply of its own. If the full report is no longer available, the job still uses the short preview. [Scheduled job payloads](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/payloads)
  [#185985](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185985).

  Thanks [@masatohoshino](https://github.com/masatohoshino), [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Prevents Doctor from silently dropping malformed heartbeat hours during migration to automations. If Doctor flags a heartbeat time, correct it to `HH:MM` and rerun `openclaw doctor --fix` to migrate the intended schedule.
  [issue #186218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/186218) · [Doctor migration guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/doctor/config-migrations).

  [#186305](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186305).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), [@nxmxbbd](https://github.com/nxmxbbd) (report).
- Fixes Doctor and update checks getting blocked by a recreated `HEARTBEAT.md` after that heartbeat has already moved to an automation. Doctor flags the file for review without opening it.
  [issue #186185](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/186185) · [Heartbeat guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/heartbeat).

  [#186307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186307).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), [@nxmxbbd](https://github.com/nxmxbbd) (report).
- Restores skill guidance in scheduled routines that were missing their eligible skills even though they could read the instructions. Stops Code Mode from listing skills it cannot read.
  [issue #186285](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/186285) · [Skills guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skills).

  [#186306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186306).

  Thanks [@giodl73-repo](https://github.com/giodl73-repo), [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) (co-author).
- Clarifies why a reminder was rejected if its delivery destination was left blank or a one-time schedule included a trigger. The error confirms that nothing was saved and tells you how to retry. Omit or fill a blank destination, remove the trigger for a one-time reminder, or choose a recurring schedule.
  [Reminder troubleshooting](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/troubleshooting).

  [#186354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186354).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), [@tobyqu](https://github.com/tobyqu) (report), [@latter-bolden](https://github.com/latter-bolden) (fleet evidence), [@gaozixiang1](https://github.com/gaozixiang1) (earlier safeguard), [@lanzhi-lee](https://github.com/lanzhi-lee) (earlier safeguard).
- Fixes scheduled runs showing only a stale tool-failure warning after recovering and recording a meaningful result.
  [#186652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186652).

  Thanks steipete.
- Replaces the error banner for invalid cron expressions and time zones with a message under the affected field. Create and Save stay unavailable until the value is corrected.
  [#186724](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186724).

  Thanks jondihaynes and obviyus.
- Fixes operator-created [automations](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/managing-jobs) being hidden from the conversation that owns them, so you can find, pause, resume, reschedule, run or remove them from that conversation. Changing what runs or where results go makes the job run with the owner account’s permissions instead of the operator’s. If the job has no account on record, those edits still need a Gateway owner or operator.
  [#187195](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187195).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Prevents an unmet scheduled automation condition from posting a “did not start” notice or moving the conversation to the top.
  [#188594](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188594), [#188700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188700).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa) for the release backports (d1a8134 and 26a71f5).
- Preserves the catch-up delay for missed agent jobs when the scheduler restarts without restarting the Gateway.
  [#191838](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191838).

  Thanks [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa).
- Lets OpenClaw reclaim an idle cron worker under memory pressure when automatic scheduling is off. Manual job runs still work.
  [#196387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196387), [openclaw/openclaw@08f5c5f5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/08f5c5f5870ea669a725c6bdb42af7c02ef62478).

  Thanks [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa), [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).
- Fixes Automation settings showing triggers as off when you have left them at the default. The control shows “Default: On,” and you can return to that default without saving an explicit On setting.
  [Source commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bc4a01b1fa411b430e26b4c57936ded931ea5762).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and [@nkeil](https://github.com/nkeil).
- Stops queued scheduled runs from using owner-private memory if the requester loses owner access before the run starts.
  [Commit 33e52df](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/33e52df4cd03e9e6a7d30849c702b45196aa5883) (combined release backport).

  Thanks [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa) and [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus) for the backport, and [@zeroaltitude](https://github.com/zeroaltitude).
- Fixes scheduled runs losing access to the originating conversation’s workspace, memory, or board after you edit a message, switch branches, or reset the conversation that created them. Scheduled operator continuations and plugin commands follow the current conversation, and results meant for that conversation reach it, including in WebChat when no external destination is set. Jobs that depend on an archived or deleted conversation or a missing worktree still pause, and Doctor can report why.
  [Commit 623fd6d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/623fd6dad99d7feaf1945cd631fc8202238c51f2), [Commit 94e1bfb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/94e1bfbba5aeb1aaf76edfa9393a13f2bca71331).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus), [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc), [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa).
- Restores cron’s link to its jobs or run history after a legacy store has already moved, when only one retained set remains.
  [Commit fdadb27](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fdadb276ef02acf11135aa78b354f44f38c91098).

  Thanks [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa), [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).
- Prevents [scheduled jobs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/delivery) that use global sessions from picking up another agent’s recipient, account or thread when falling back to a saved destination.
  original repair.

  [#173855](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173855), [#156970](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156970).

  Thanks steipete.
- Fixes missing failure alerts when a recurring automation is disabled after ten failed runs in a row. OpenClaw sends the disable notice through an eligible configured failure destination without needing the model to respond. If there’s no eligible destination, it queues the notice for the owning agent.
  [Automation delivery](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/delivery).

  [#174309](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174309).

  Thanks [@saftall](https://github.com/saftall).
- Fixes scheduled jobs failing on their first save with PostgreSQL.
  [#174786](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174786).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Keeps older periodic-task heartbeat instructions out of the conversation history an agent uses after the heartbeat has finished, including turns that ended silently.
  [#174815](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174815).

  Thanks [@maliv2](https://github.com/maliv2), [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Replaces confusing errors with a message that tells you who can edit an automation’s prompt or tools when your chat doesn’t have permission. For an automation with no recorded owner, only a Gateway owner or operator can make those edits. Chat can still enable, disable, reschedule, or remove it where it already has permission.
  [#175153](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175153).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Stops Doctor from replacing a legacy automation’s explicitly linked shared account with the default during migration. If the linked account is missing or cannot run unattended, Doctor warns and leaves the automation unchanged.
  [#175165](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175165).

  Thanks [@fuller-stack-dev](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev).
- Fixes [background command follow-ups](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/background-process) getting dropped after an isolated cron run ends. A completion already queued while the run was active waits its turn and follows up in that run’s session, not the main chat. Completions not accepted before the run ends remain suppressed, and jobs configured for no delivery still don’t follow up automatically.
  [Issue #176235](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176235).

  [#176511](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176511).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and [@elikampf](https://github.com/elikampf).
- Fixes [Doctor lint](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/doctor/running) checking the wrong agent or missing a `HEARTBEAT.md` that would block repair or an update on setups with legacy heartbeat settings. It checks the configured agents’ actual files, including with `--all`.
  [#186926](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186926).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and [@nxmxbbd](https://github.com/nxmxbbd) for [the report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/186862).
- Fixes [Doctor](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/doctor/config-migrations) turning a disabled heartbeat into an enabled Proactive check and leaving the migration unfinished. Doctor also repairs unfinished migrations when it can confirm the heartbeat was disabled. If it cannot tell, it leaves the automation alone and tells you how to finish the repair.
  [#181659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181659).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and to [@Marvinthebored](https://github.com/Marvinthebored) for the report.
- Fixes plain [heartbeat checklists](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/heartbeat) under a `tasks:` line blocking Gateway startup during migration. Doctor keeps those checklists as notes without scheduling them. If a real task declaration is incomplete, the update check flags it and Doctor leaves the original `HEARTBEAT.md` in place for repair.
  [#181842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181842).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and to [@nxmxbbd](https://github.com/nxmxbbd) for the report and co-authorship.
- Preserves valid conversation permissions when Doctor repairs an automation’s model account binding.
  [#182262](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182262).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes scheduled automations losing eligible owner-only tools on CLI backends that were available on the embedded runtime. If the requester loses owner access during a run, the automation can no longer keep acting as that owner. Older operator-linked trusted-policy jobs without a saved requester and with a direct-chat parent can read that chat’s owner-private memory. Doctor’s scheduled-run review shows which CLI jobs gain owner-only tools and which jobs lose them because their requester is no longer an owner.
  [#182585](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182585).

  Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).
- Fixes older Cron run history becoming unavailable when a new run starts a fresh session while the older messages are being checked. The history still isn’t shared if access was revoked.
  [Final verification repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/be8e76f13738ef16f443b2c6cb99c4d98d632970), [sharing preparation follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/75812b5d1e2475910db6327e5973b915b0d1e300).

  Thanks [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa) and [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).
- Fixes automation updates and row expansion failing while the Control UI is still loading session details.
  [Commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9afcc1b7b29a51535771a09747556970f6fbdfbd).

  Thanks [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa) and [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).
- Fixes scheduled prompts showing in full when an automation continues an existing conversation in the Control UI. Runs with enough detail appear as compact automation activity, and older recorded prompts without those details move into a notice you can expand. The agent’s replies and your own messages stay visible.
  [#181035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181035).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Prevents cron history errors from revealing session keys to callers who cannot access them.
  [#172807](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172807).

  Watcher approval timing is covered in [Watcher approval timing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d90406afff0dc32e5f6cb76dfc3b1a9d9f8422ae). Save retries were addressed separately.

  [#182262](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182262).

  [Commit c12366a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c12366a42c46360eaf0da5df6036085a0976eb58).

  [Commit 28ebe54](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/28ebe54da16719b29f6d074821e1cc97a8c5852f).
- Fixes `openclaw cron list` and `show`, and cron or automation `run --wait`, ignoring Ctrl-C or SIGTERM while waiting. Interrupting `run --wait` stops the wait, not the queued job. An add or edit already sent still reports its result and is not undone by an interrupt.
  List and show · Run wait · [Cron commands](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/cron).

  [#187726](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187726), [#186750](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186750).

  Thanks [@SunnyShu0925](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925), [@alix-007](https://github.com/Alix-007) and [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Fixes automation searches missing jobs, and cron run-history searches missing job names, summaries or errors, when accented text is typed and stored in different forms. Saved automation names and descriptions stay unchanged.
  Automation search · Cron history search · [Cron commands](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/cron).

  [#186794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186794), [#187024](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187024).

- Keeps [scheduled checks](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/payloads) out of chat when they report no change, including an unchanged known blocker. The desktop and mobile automation views keep the last meaningful result and show when the job was checked and whether that check failed. Meaningful results stay in the persistent conversation where the automation runs even when external notifications are off.
  [#182262](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182262).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Fixes default cron jobs and their history disappearing after you move the state directory while OpenClaw is stopped or restore a backup to a new location. If OpenClaw cannot identify the default schedule in an older store, jobs pause until you run `openclaw doctor --fix` interactively and choose the default partition. The deferred choice no longer blocks the [Doctor](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/doctor) update check. If retired heartbeat settings remain, complete the [Doctor migration](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/doctor/config-migrations#heartbeat-to-ordinary-automations) before starting the Gateway. See [cron troubleshooting](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/troubleshooting).
  [#183508](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183508), [#184497](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184497).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), [@shakkernerd](https://github.com/shakkernerd).

#### Browser and Computer Use

Browser page triage can assess whether a page is loading, empty or blocked. The selected Decision provider receives a page excerpt.




##### Browser page triage


Use a Decision model to assess browser page blockers and find updates to voice, media and meeting workflows. Browser triage sends a page excerpt to the selected provider and its result is advisory.

Your agent can ask a Decision model whether a browser tab is still loading, has no results, or is showing a blocker such as a login screen or paywall. This advisory judgment works on supported text-capable Chromium and Lightpanda profiles, and an incomplete page reading can mislead it. The selected Decision provider receives a page excerpt, and hosted inference can incur charges. See [Decision models](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/decision-models) and [supported browser profiles](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/browser/lightweight#page-classification-and-judge).
Browser judge action · [Request #179360](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/179360).

[#179362](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179362).

Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).

#### Plugins and Integrations

Plugins can show interactive results in chat, delegate work to native subagents and connect to GitHub. Enabled user-installed plugins can show native UI with the signed-in viewer’s Gateway permissions.




##### Decisions for plugins


Plugin developers can ask a supported Decision model to score or rank options, and the model can decline to answer instead of being forced to guess. Decision V2 also supports per-question errors and, where the provider offers them, sorting, tags and image questions. [OpenRouter Jev](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/openrouter#typed-decisions-with-jev) can evaluate a PNG or JPEG, and Jev 1.14 and its latest alias can return a bounding box. Image and box support are experimental. See the [Decision SDK guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/sdk-overview/capabilities.md).

If a previously working Decision call is blocked, check that the plugin allows the chosen model. Images are sent to the selected provider.
The model manifest covers capabilities and pricing; the next change covers model allowlists.

[#156554](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156554), [#156621](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156621).

See [Model manifest capabilities and pricing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/manifest/models.md).

[#157148](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157148), [#157225](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157225), [#157492](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157492).

Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).

[#175070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175070).

Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).




##### Interactive plugin views


Review Skill Workshop drafts before applying them and use new plugin capabilities in chat. Enabled user-installed plugins can show native UI by default, with the signed-in viewer’s permissions and no sandbox. To turn that off, set gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlugins to false and reload open Control UI tabs. If you used Claws, update old commands, links, configuration and Gateway API calls to use Templates.

Compatible plugins can show interactive views beneath tool results in Control UI chat. Views return when you scroll back through history without rerunning the tool, and a saved text summary remains available when the view cannot be displayed.

Enabled user-installed plugins can show native UI by default, including plugins enabled before this update. Native UI runs without a sandbox in each signed-in viewer’s browser with that viewer’s Gateway permissions. Existing opt-outs remain in effect. To turn it off for user-installed plugins, set `gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlugins` to `false` and reload open Control UI tabs. The catalog warns before installation, and plugin details and enable reviews identify native UI.
[#173135](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173135).

Thanks [@jacobtomlinson](https://github.com/jacobtomlinson), [@Patrick-Erichsen](https://github.com/Patrick-Erichsen).

[#177869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177869).

Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).

- [Feature plugin guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/feature-plugins.md) · [Plugin surfaces](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/manifest/surfaces.md) · [Inline incident example](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/examples/inline-incident/README.md) · [Native plugin UI guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.5/docs/plugins/feature-plugins.md).
- Markdown exports and catalog or Beam mirrors carry the text summary. Native HTML exports keep the view record and require its plugin renderer.




##### Plugin reloads


Your agent can keep working through a plugin reload when the plugin opts in to [continuing active turns](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime#reload-safe-plugins). Running tool calls finish before the turn moves to the reloaded plugin, including for compatible context engines. A plugin that has not opted in waits for the whole turn. Reload status shows which plugins can hand over and which are keeping a reload waiting.
[#185315](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185315).

- Context-engine handover ([#185544](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185544)). Context engines must save turn state durably; a turn ends with an error if the replacement no longer provides its configured engine.
- Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).




##### Read-only Codex connected apps


Codex plugins can look things up in connected apps with read-only access. Set `read_only: true` for the plugin to allow only enabled tools that are explicitly classified as read-only. Existing approvals still apply. A shared app stays restricted if any enabled plugin requires read-only access, and scheduled tasks keep the restriction they were created with even if you relax the setting later. [Codex native plugin configuration](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/codex-native-plugins#destructive-action-policy)
Limits a Codex plugin’s connected apps to enabled tools classified as read-only. [issue #180029](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180029).

[#180030](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180030).

Thanks [@Kimiyu-186](https://github.com/Kimiyu-186).




##### Plugin-owned model credentials


Provider plugins can use credentials they manage for model requests. Requests remain tied to the owning plugin and are blocked if that authority is revoked or replaced. See the [provider plugin guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins.md).
Plugin-owned routes use their owner’s credentials exclusively. OpenAI Responses requests with these credentials use guarded HTTP.

[#156799](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156799).

Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc) and [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).




##### Native subagents for plugins


Plugin authors can delegate work to native subagents under the requester’s permissions and collect the results. [Eligible reply handlers](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime/background-work#requester-bound-native-children) and authenticated commands can use this path, and commands can find recently recorded children if they finish later. Reusable profiles can provide instructions, limit inherited tool access and require a result format. See [plugin background work](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime/background-work#recover-plugin-owned-native-children).
Adds opt-in native subagents for authenticated commands and optional requested and resolved settings on native results.

Adds a lookup for up to 200 recent children recorded for the same plugin, requester and conversation. Listing, starting and collecting children require access to the native results tool.

[#180173](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180173), [#180274](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180274).

Thanks [@fuller-stack-dev](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev).
[Manifest capabilities](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/manifest/capabilities)

[#181292](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181292).

Thanks [@fuller-stack-dev](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev).
Requester-bound native delegation and collection for plugins in.

[#175276](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175276).

Thanks [@fuller-stack-dev](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev).




##### Agent Guidance


The optional Agent Guidance plugin lets you keep shared instructions in one place and give them to selected agents. Keep the files outside agent-writable workspaces and use access controls for enforcement, since a failed reload can leave turns without this guidance.
Enable `agent-guidance`, grant its prompt-injection and conversation-access hook permissions, and select the agent IDs that receive the files. Reload the plugin or restart after editing them.

Shared instruction files for selected agents.

[#173602](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173602).

Thanks [@giodl73-repo](https://github.com/giodl73-repo), [@Patrick-Erichsen](https://github.com/Patrick-Erichsen).

  [#185945](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185945).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).

  [#186147](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186147).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces the temporary memory needed to check plugin session actions, such as activity panel refreshes. Rejects action data with too many fields before reading their values.
  [#186236](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186236).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Adds an optional hook for channel plugins to send a best-effort notice after a message has permanently failed.

  [#186289](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186289).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Adds `readSqliteDatabaseWriteRevision` so plugins can read the in-process SQLite write revision without issuing a query.
  [Source commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e8a7c1fb91c8a220b0aa3941ee5e1de830457b07).
- Adds a guarded HTTP helper for provider plugins that reuses OpenClaw’s model connection policy. Release the response in `finally`; the helper supplies neither credentials nor request authority. [Provider plugin SDK guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins)
  HTTP helper.

  [#174002](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174002), [Provider HTTP SDK commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4aa78569f23d1787235a624d462d7afcfe993245).

  Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).
- Reduces the work of preparing conversation history for plugin hooks, especially in long conversations. Nested message content passed to `before_prompt_build` and `agent_turn_prepare` is read-only. Return a hook contribution to change the prompt, or copy the content before editing it for your plugin’s own use. [Prompt-hook migration](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration#prompt-hook-history-is-read-only)
  [#182239](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182239), [#182349](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182349), [#184337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184337), [#184376](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184376).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces database work when plugins save several pieces of state together, poll unchanged state or repeatedly register keys that are still in use. Reads continue to reflect committed updates, including Doctor repairs. [Plugin state reference](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime/state-and-system)
  [#183400](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183400), [#183844](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183844), [#186230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186230).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Updates the [provider guides](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/model-catalogs) with live model discovery and advertised thinking-level guidance, and adds a [contribution checklist](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins#checklist-before-you-open-a-provider-pr) for connection setup, documentation and testing with a real agent turn.
  Model discovery and thinking levels · Provider checklist

  [#187214](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187214), [#187362](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187362).

  Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Keeps the synchronous memory `status()` fallback for third-party managers through December 31, 2026. Migrate to `statusAsync` before its removal in the first January 2027 stable release. [SQLite SDK migration guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/sdk-migration/sqlite-async.md)
  [Status migration commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8c96ef749f451f534f341a53d5da96d477fb4140).
- Updates the [plugin SDK contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.5/docs/plugins/sdk-migration.md) without a compatibility window. If your plugin registers a session-keyed run, move `setActiveEmbeddedRun` into the host-admitted `runAttempt` and retain its cleanup function. Replace `chatAbortControllers` and `chatQueuedTurns` with authenticated Gateway method calls, and read `startDeadlineAtMs` instead of `expiresAtMs` in start-owner observations.
  [#175837](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175837).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).
- Adds a deprecation warning when a plugin calls the built-in memory manager’s synchronous `status()`. Switch to `statusAsync()` using the [SQLite SDK migration guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/sqlite-async). The synchronous call remains available through December 31, 2026, with removal planned for the first January 2027 stable release after the warning and replacement have shipped in stable.
  [#175199](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175199).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Removes `normalizeWhitespace` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/web-content-extractor`. If your plugin imports it from that path, replace that import.
  [#178569](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178569).

  Thanks [@HeZ2z](https://github.com/HeZ2z), [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Changes after-tool plugin hooks so editing a tool result can affect what OpenClaw shows later. Treat those results as read-only.
  [#174838](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174838).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Removes the automatic skip for [`before_prompt_build` hooks](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session) that call themselves on the same runner. If you write one of these hooks, avoid calling it recursively.
  [#174872](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174872).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Changes delayed plugin cleanup so it can read or clear newer temporary plugin state when the same context keys are reused. When a hook and an instance of the same plugin report the same error object during cleanup, it can appear as one failure instead of two.
  [#174872](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174872).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Adds [Gemini Decision 1](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/decision-models) for yes-or-no questions, choices and scores based on text, JSON or a supported image. Select `google/gemini-decision-1` with a Gemini Developer API key. Evaluation sends the supplied evidence to Google at Gemini API rates. Chat model discovery no longer removes Decision-only models from the selection for evaluations.
  The released change was adapted from [#197501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197501) and the [upstream commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0182580ebf7e1436686791f263f49a5dae52df0a). The upstream commit names Ayaan Zaidi as author.

  [Released adaptation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01b98da7d3dbcca5d26a6a970f1ab0438adfdcab).

  Thanks to released co-authors [@RomneyDa](https://github.com/RomneyDa), [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc) and [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).
- Adds Decision SDK V2 support for the existing [local ONNX classifier](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/onnx) without an API key. A compatible host and plugin pairing is required. The adapter handles Boolean, choice and score questions on text or JSON, and V1 calls still work.
  [#174162](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174162).

  Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc), [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Adds an [SDK option](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-overview/capabilities#decision-models-contract-version-1) for plugins to mark evaluations as optional.
  [#174266](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174266).

  Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).
- Adds [custom channel settings views](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/feature-plugins#packaged-settings-presentations), so plugin authors can customize Control UI settings pages for their channels while OpenClaw handles configuration editing and account access. Nostr’s existing profile editor moves into its plugin, while remaining in the same place for users. A Settings-only plugin view also lets the existing Memory overview load without starting Memory Core’s runtime UI.
  Channel settings views and the Memory Settings view.

  [#176042](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176042), [#174452](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174452).

  Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc).
- Avoids reading a saved diff back just to find out when it was created or expires. Plugin authors can also get those timestamps when registering a new stored item without changing code that uses the existing yes-or-no registration method. See the [plugin storage guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime/state-and-system).
  [#174081](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174081).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

  [#175231](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175231).

  [#175829](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175829).

  Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

ClawRouter requires Decisions support on the service; legacy V1 requests remain limited to 256 questions. [Decision limits](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/decision-models)
